structure:
repos/trade-imports-stub is a small Java / Spring Boot service that stands in for third-party integrations on the local stack, in the fit suites and in CDP perf runs. About 100 files: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports holds stubs/federated (an address lookup simulator plus Entra and STS token simulators for the EUDPA-390 address lookup spike, about 500 lines), stubs/mdm (CountriesController and PortsOfEntryController with their MdmCountry, MdmBlock, MdmSubDivision, MdmCodedValue, MdmPortsResponse and MdmPortOfEntry records, about 180 lines), stubs/trade (the Trade Platform OAuth token stub), utils/FileUtils, and cross-cutting latency, faults, filter, configuration, tls, metrics and exception packages. src/main/resources/responses holds the two MDM fixtures: countriesResponse.json (772 lines) and portsOfEntryResponse.json (82 lines, 78 ports). application.yml (152 lines) configures the address lookup simulator's audience and the MDM latency profile. Tests mirror the main tree (AddressLookupSimulatorControllerTest 194 lines, FileUtilsTest 77 lines). There is no rulings ledger. The scope takes in only the address lookup simulator (the searches it answers, the addresses it returns and their postcodes, and the bearer check that gates them) and the MDM countries and ports stubs (what they return, their fields and how the blocks parameter is handled). It leaves out the Entra and STS simulators' token issuing, the trade token stub, the latency profiles and fault injection (perf-test tooling, not look and feel), and the Mongo, AWS, TLS, metrics, logging and CI configuration. The scoped code is about 1,600 lines in two independent features, cut into two parts along that seam.

Extracted in 2 parts:
Part 1, Address lookup simulator: Part 1, Address lookup simulator. Read in full: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/stubs/federated/AddressLookupSimulatorController.java (163 lines: one GET endpoint, a bearer check, a switch over reserved search terms, a 401 body, a three-address fixture and a no-results fixture), src/test/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/stubs/federated/AddressLookupSimulatorControllerTest.java (194 lines, 14 MockMvc tests), the EUDPA-390 block of src/main/resources/application.yml (lines 106 to 119: sts-simulator settings, out of scope, and address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience), README.md (72 lines: latency profiles and fault injection for trade-token and mdm only; it never mentions the address lookup simulator) and docs/repos/trade-imports-stub.md in the workspace (no mention of address, lookup or simulator). Covered: the endpoint path and its postcode and find parameters with postcode precedence, the 400 when neither is sent, every reserved term (SW1A 1AA, ZZ1 1ZZ, QQ1 1QQ, XX1 1XX, YY1 1YY, TT1 1TT, Buckingham Palace, Downing Street) and the default no-results answer, the three fixture addresses field by field and the header, the recorded reasons for the fixture shape and for not modelling find, the bearer check in general terms with its 401 body, the expected-audience setting, and every test. Gaps recorded: no documentation of the simulator in the README or the workspace repo page, the truncation and find fixtures the class comment defers to iteration 2, and no fixture for a non-London, Welsh, Scottish or Northern Irish postcode.
Part 2, MDM countries and ports stubs: Part 2 of repo:stub, MDM countries and ports stubs. Read in full: stubs/mdm/countries (CountriesController, 34 lines, and the MdmCountry, MdmBlock, MdmSubDivision and MdmCodedValue records), stubs/mdm/poe (PortsOfEntryController, 32 lines, and the MdmPortsResponse and MdmPortOfEntry records), utils/FileUtils (30 lines) and FileUtilsTest (77 lines, 5 tests), the two fixtures responses/countriesResponse.json (772 lines, 31 country records, every field read) and responses/portsOfEntryResponse.json (82 lines, 78 ports), the mdm block of application.yml (lines 139 to 152) and the MDM rows of README.md's latency and fault tables (lines 11 to 16 and 40 to 43). Layout: two GET endpoints, each answers with a classpath JSON fixture loaded per request through FileUtils, with a fixed trace header; neither filters on its query parameters. Covered: both endpoints' paths, the required subscription-key header, the system and blocks parameters and what the stub does with them, the response header and wrapper, every record field, every country (one claim each, with codes, long name, subdivisions and block), the fixture-wide values (one block, independence, status, system), all 78 ports in fixture order with their duplicates and copy oddities, FileUtils' loading and failure behaviour, every FileUtilsTest test, the MDM latency metadata for the two paths, the README's MDM rows, and gaps against what the live-animals and germinal-products journeys need from countries and ports (block membership, non-European countries, port type and commodity designation, subdivision blocs, controller tests). Latency profiles and fault injection themselves are left to their out-of-scope tooling; the address lookup simulator is part 1.

claims.statement: The stub simulates the DEFRA address lookup gateway's address search at GET /simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses.
The simulator stands in for the address lookup gateway that the INS backend calls, as part of the EUDPA-390 address lookup spike.
claims.quote: # EUDPA-390 address lookup spike — the three federated-credential simulators (plan Step 6).
claims.note: The caller being ins-backend is stated in the application.yml comment at line 115: "The audience ins-backend's Entra token request resolves to".

claims.statement: The search accepts two optional query parameters: postcode and find (free text).
claims.quote:
@RequestParam(required = false) String postcode,
        @RequestParam(required = false) String find

claims.statement: When both postcode and find are sent, postcode is used and find is ignored.
claims.quote: String term = postcode != null ? postcode : find;

claims.statement: A postcode and a find term are matched the same way, against the same reserved terms: the simulator deliberately does not model what find really matches (a postcode, building name or number, street or town), leaving that to the real gateway in dev.
claims.quote: Deliberately identical for both parameters. What find really matches — a postcode, a building name or number, a street, a town — is a question only the real gateway can answer, and a simulator that guessed would look like an answer. Local runs prove the plumbing carries the parameter through; dev settles the behaviour.

claims.statement: When neither postcode nor find is sent, the simulator answers 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Either postcode or find is required".

Reserved terms are matched exactly, case and spacing included, so a postcode sent in lower case or without its space (for example sw1a 1aa or SW1A1AA) does not hit a fixture and gets the no-results answer.
claims.note: Inferred from the Java string switch, which compares exactly, and the default branch returning NO_RESULTS_FIXTURE. Whether callers normalise the postcode before sending it is outside this source.

claims.statement: Searching for postcode SW1A 1AA returns 200 with a JSON body holding the three fixture addresses.
Searching for postcode ZZ1 1ZZ returns 204 No Content with no body: the reserved no-results postcode.
Searching for postcode QQ1 1QQ returns 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Requested postcode is not valid": the reserved invalid postcode.
Searching for postcode XX1 1XX returns 503 with a JSON body whose message is "Service Unavailable": the reserved throttled or unavailable postcode.
Searching for postcode YY1 1YY returns 200 with an HTML body ("Bad Gateway") instead of JSON: the reserved proxy-error postcode.
Searching for postcode TT1 1TT waits 15 seconds, then returns 200 with the three fixture addresses: the reserved slow-response postcode.
The free-text terms "Buckingham Palace" and "Downing Street" each return 200 with the three fixture addresses, so the find search can be demonstrated locally.
A result for a reserved free-text term says nothing about whether the same search would return results from the real gateway: the free-text terms are fixtures, not a model of find.
claims.quote: These are reserved terms like the postcodes above, NOT a model of what find matches — that is the question the spike exists to answer, and only the real gateway can. A search here returning results says nothing about whether the same search would return results in dev.

claims.statement: Every other postcode or free-text term returns 200 with a JSON body holding no results: header totalResults "0" and an empty results list.
Every successful JSON answer has a header object with totalResults, given as a string ("3" or "0"), and a results list.
Each address result has the fields addressLine, subBuildingName, buildingName, buildingNumber, street, town, postcode, country, uprn, match, matchDescription and language, and no county field.

claims.statement: Address values are all upper case, country is free text ("ENGLAND") rather than an ISO code, and match, uprn and buildingNumber are strings.
claims.quote: everything upper case, {@code country} free text rather than an ISO code, no county field, {@code match} a string, and counts as strings.

claims.statement: All three fixture addresses share postcode SW1A 1AA and town LONDON, whichever reserved term returned them, including the free-text terms.
The fixtures follow the real gateway's dev response of 17 September 2026, not the published v2.1 specification.
claims.quote: Shaped like the real dev response of 2026-09-17, not like the published v2.1 specification

claims.statement: The three fixture addresses are the three ways a name lands in a result (the whole name in subBuildingName; a building number and street; a sub-building, building name and street), chosen because they make composing address line 1 awkward; the Buckingham Palace case is the one dev actually returned.
claims.quote: The three results are the three ways a name lands, which is what makes composing address line 1 awkward — the first is the Buckingham Palace case dev actually returned, where {@code subBuildingName} carries the whole name and {@code buildingName}, {@code buildingNumber} and {@code street} are all null.

claims.statement: Every search requires a bearer token: the simulator checks the authorisation scheme, the token's signature, its audience and its expiry before answering any search, the way a real resource server would.
claims.quote: Checks the bearer token the way a real resource server would — signature, audience, expiry — before serving the reserved-postcode fixtures
claims.note: Described in general terms only, as the brief requires.

claims.statement: A search with a missing or invalid bearer token is refused with 401 and the JSON body { "statusCode": 401, "message": "Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid." }, word for word what the real gateway returned in dev on 17 September 2026.
claims.quote: .body("{ \"statusCode\": 401, \"message\": \"Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid.\" }");

claims.statement: The 401 answer carries no WWW-Authenticate header, matching the real gateway.
claims.quote: The gateway sends no {@code WWW-Authenticate} header with it, and neither does this.

claims.statement: The bearer check runs before the search terms are looked at, so an unauthorised request gets 401 even when it sends no search term or a reserved term.

The audience the simulator expects is set by address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience, overridable with ADDRESS_LOOKUP_SIMULATOR_EXPECTED_AUDIENCE, and must match the INS backend's local and stack Scope value exactly, api:// prefix included.
claims.quote:
# The audience ins-backend's Entra token request resolves to once /.default is stripped — must
  # match the local/stack "Scope" value in the EUDPA-390 plan exactly, api:// prefix included.
claims.note: The default value is a placeholder identifier, not a secret, and is not repeated here.

claims.statement: The simulator, like the real gateway in dev, accepts only the api:// form of the audience and refuses a token whose audience is the bare identifier.
claims.quote:
# The real gateway policy in dev wants the api:// form and rejects the bare GUID, so this does
  # too: a simulator that accepted either would not have caught the 401 the spike hit.

claims.statement: Test addresses_shouldReturnThreeFixtureAddresses_forTheDefaultPostcode proves SW1A 1AA returns 200 JSON with totalResults "3" and DOWNING STREET in the body.
Test addresses_shouldReturnAddressesShapedLikeTheRealApi proves the result carries subBuildingName BUCKINGHAM PALACE, country ENGLAND, match as the string "1", and no county.
claims.quote: // The divergences from the published specification that dev confirmed on 2026-09-17.

claims.statement: Test addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerAudienceIsTheBareGuidRatherThanTheApiUri proves a bare-identifier audience gets 401 with the exact gateway body and no WWW-Authenticate header.
claims.quote:
// The exact mismatch the spike hit in dev: the scope requested as the bare GUID produces
        // this audience, and the gateway policy wants the api:// form.

claims.statement: The missing WWW-Authenticate header on the gateway's 401 means a caller cannot rely on Spring's own authorisation failure handler to evict a stale token.
claims.quote:
// The real gateway sends none, which is why Spring's own authorization failure handler
            // cannot be used to evict a stale token (plan, iteration 1 gaps).

claims.statement: Test addresses_shouldServeTheReservedFreeTextTerms_soFindCanBeDemonstrated proves find=Buckingham Palace returns 200 with BUCKINGHAM PALACE in the body.
Test addresses_shouldReturnNoResults_forFreeTextThatIsNotReserved proves a partial free-text term (find=Buckingham) returns 200 with totalResults "0".
claims.quote: // The reserved terms are fixtures, not a model of what find matches.

claims.statement: Test addresses_shouldReturn400_whenNeitherPostcodeNorFindIsGiven proves a search with no term returns 400 with "Either postcode or find is required".
Test addresses_shouldReturn204_forTheReservedNoResultsPostcode proves ZZ1 1ZZ returns 204.
Test addresses_shouldReturnARejectedPostcode400_forTheReservedInvalidPostcode proves QQ1 1QQ returns 400 with "Requested postcode" in the body.
Test addresses_shouldReturn503_forTheReservedThrottledPostcode proves XX1 1XX returns 503.
Test addresses_shouldReturnNonJsonHtml_forTheReservedProxyErrorPostcode proves YY1 1YY returns 200 with an HTML content type.

Tests addresses_shouldReject_whenNoBearerPresent, addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerAudienceIsWrong, addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerHasExpired and addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerSignatureIsWrong prove a search is refused with 401 when the bearer is missing, has the wrong audience, has expired or is signed with the wrong key.
No test proves the TT1 1TT 15-second delayed answer, the XX1 1XX and YY1 1YY bodies, the Downing Street free-text term, or that postcode wins when both postcode and find are sent.
The simulator has no fixtures for truncated result sets or for find-specific matching; the class comment defers them to iteration 2.
claims.quote: Only the fixtures iteration 1 needs are wired here; {@code find} and the truncation/find fixtures are iteration 2.
claims.note: Inferred as still unbuilt: the switch at lines 60-76 has no truncation fixture, though the reserved free-text terms show find is partly wired.

claims.statement: The stub has no fixture address outside London or outside England (no Welsh, Scottish or Northern Irish address and no language other than EN), so an address lookup page cannot be exercised locally with such an address.
Neither the stub's README nor the workspace's docs/repos/trade-imports-stub.md documents the address lookup simulator, its path or its reserved postcodes; they are recorded only in the code.

claims.statement: The stub answers GET /mdm/geo/countries, standing in for MDM's countries reference-data call.
The countries endpoint requires an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key request header; Spring rejects a request without it, so a call with no key is refused (a bad request) rather than answered.
claims.note: The header is required by default (@RequestHeader with no required=false). The 400 outcome is Spring's default for a missing required header, not code in the stub.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint accepts any subscription-key value: the key is read but never checked, so any non-empty value gets the full answer.
claims.note: Inferred because the method body never uses ocpApimSubscriptionKey.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint takes an optional system query parameter but ignores it: the same list comes back whatever system is asked for.
claims.note: Inferred because the method body never uses system.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint takes an optional blocks query parameter but does not filter on it: every call returns the whole fixture, whichever block is asked for or if none is.
claims.note: Inferred because blocks is never read in the method body. Outside this slice, trade-imports-reference-data's MdmService passes system GBNAG and blocks to MDM and then filters the answer by block itself (isIncludedInRequestedBlock), so on the stack the filtering a user sees is done by reference-data, not by the stub.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint answers 200 OK with a JSON array of country records read from responses/countriesResponse.json.
The countries endpoint sets the response header x-ms-middleware-request-id to the fixed value stub-trace-id.

Each country record carries name, longName, effectiveAlpha2, effectiveAlpha3, effectiveAlias, effectiveLongName, independent (a boolean), statusName, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, systemLongName, a list of subDivisions and a list of blocks.
A country's block membership is a record of the block name, an includeCountry boolean and a list of string tags.
A subdivision record carries a code (an object holding a single value string), a name and a list of blocs (spelt blocs, not blocks).
The countries fixture holds 31 country records, in alphabetical order of name from Austria to Switzerland, so the stub always returns these 31 countries in that order.
claims.note: Counted with jq (length 31). Records 012 to 042 name each one.

claims.statement: Port ids are the strings "1" to "78", numbered in fixture order with no gaps.

The ports come roughly in alphabetical order of name but not strictly: HES Humber Bulk Terminal comes before Harwich Port, TILBURY before Teesside International Airport, and Port of Middlesbrough after Portsmouth  Port, so a page listing them in fixture order would not be fully alphabetical.
claims.note: Inferred by reading the order; the first two exceptions match a case-sensitive sort, the Middlesbrough one matches no sort.

claims.statement: Every port is in Great Britain: every code starts with GB, and the list mixes airports (such as Heathrow Airport), seaports and harbours (such as Port of Dover) and docks (such as Liverpool Docks).
Pembroke Port appears twice, under codes GB PED (id 46) and GB PEM (id 47), so a port list built from the stub shows two identical names.
Port of Sheerness appears twice, under code GBSHS with no space (id 63) and GB SHS (id 64), so a port list built from the stub shows two identical names.
The port name "Portsmouth  Port" has two spaces between its words.
Tilbury appears three times with different names and codes: "TILBURY" in capitals (GB TIL), "Tilbury 2 Ro-Ro Terminal" (GB TILR) and "Tilbury Port" (GB TILL).
Port 76 (GB TEE) is named "Teestort", which reads as a misspelling of Teesport.
claims.note: That it is a misspelling is inferred; the fixture spells it Teestort.

claims.statement: Both endpoints read their fixture from the classpath afresh on every request, so the answer is always the fixture's current content and nothing a caller does changes it.
claims.note: Inferred from the controllers calling getObjectFromFile inside the request handler with no caching.

claims.statement: If a fixture cannot be found or read, the stub logs "Failed to read from JSON file" and fails the request with the error "Failed to read from json file: <file name>" (a missing file is reported first as "File not found: <file name>").
claims.note: What HTTP status the caller then sees depends on the stub's exception handling, which is outside this slice.

claims.statement: A unit test proves the countries fixture reads as a non-empty list whose first country has a non-blank name and alpha-2 code.
A unit test proves Spain (ES) has exactly one subdivision, code ES-CN, named Canary Islands.
A unit test proves the ports fixture reads as a response whose result list is present and not empty.
A unit test proves the ports fixture holds exactly 78 ports, the first is GB DYC Aberdeen Airport, and the codes include GB EMA, GB EDI and GB DVR.
A unit test proves asking for a fixture that does not exist fails with an error containing "Failed to read from json file".
No test in this slice exercises the two endpoints over HTTP, so the required header, the ignored system and blocks parameters and the trace header are unproven here.
claims.ref: src/test/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports (searched with grep -rln for mdm, Countries and PortsOfEntry)
claims.note: The grep found only FileUtilsTest in scope; the other matches are the out-of-scope latency and fault tests (StubLatenciesTest, LatencyProfilesIT, FaultsIT and others), which may call these paths for their own purposes.

claims.statement: The stub's latency configuration names the MDM integration as "MDM reference data through APIM: countries and border control posts", owned by the MDM / data platform team, covering the two paths /mdm/geo/countries and /mdm/trade/bcp/poes.
claims.quote:
mdm:
      interface-name: "MDM reference data through APIM: countries and border control posts"
      owner: MDM / data platform team

claims.statement: By default the MDM paths answer with no added delay (profile zero-delay), and the interim service-level targets are p50 100 ms, p95 400 ms and p99 1,000 ms, recorded as not agreed.
claims.note: The latency profiles themselves are out of scope; this claim records only what the block says for the two MDM paths.

claims.statement: The README says the stub stands in for MDM reference data through APIM, which trade-imports-reference-data calls, on GET /mdm/geo/countries and GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes.
claims.quote:
This stub stands in for two integrations that `trade-imports-reference-data` calls, and gives each its own latency profile:
...
| `mdm` | MDM reference data through APIM | `GET /mdm/geo/countries`, `GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes` |

claims.statement: The README says both MDM paths can be made to fail on demand, for the resilience runs.
claims.note: The fault kinds and controls are out of scope.

claims.statement: The stub has no block other than GBNAG_SPS_EX and ignores the blocks parameter, so it cannot offer a germinal-products country list, or any list that differs between the live-animals and germinal-products journeys, on the local stack.
claims.note: Looked for any other block name in the fixture with jq and for any blocks handling in the controller; there is none. Whether germinal products need a different block is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: The countries fixture offers no country outside the EU and EFTA, so a live-animals or germinal-products notification from a non-European country of origin cannot be made against the stub.
claims.note: Looked at all 31 country records. Whether the journeys need non-European origins is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: Port records carry no type or transport mode (airport, seaport, road, rail), so the stub cannot narrow ports by how the consignment arrives.
claims.note: Looked at the record and all 78 fixture entries: only id, code and name. A type can only be guessed from the name.

claims.statement: Port records say nothing about which commodities a border control post is designated for (such as live animals or germinal products), so the stub cannot offer different port lists to the live-animals and germinal-products journeys.
claims.note: Looked at the record, all 78 fixture entries and the controller's parameters; there is no designation field and no filter parameter.

claims.statement: Subdivisions carry no region or block data in the fixture, so the stub cannot show whether a region such as the Canary Islands or Madeira is treated differently from its country for live animals or germinal products.
claims.note: Looked at all nine subdivision entries; none sets blocs. Whether the journeys need region-level origin is for the requirement sources to say.
